In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ligand-containing mesogens are chemo-responsive materials that undergo a transition from a thermotropic liquid crystalline to isotropic state upon the binding of metal ions.

the metal ion induced isotropic to liquid crystalline transition is not due to the formation of a metal complex with the ligand, but rather to a metal ion induced phase separation of the ligand from the mesogenic core.
the metal binding properties of liquid crystalline molecules can be tuned by varying the molecular structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metal binding to the liquid crystalline ligands results in a transition to an isotropic phase and the liquid crystallinity is retained in the absence of the metal.
we have demonstrated that metal binding can result in the disruption of liquid crystalline order in a variety of mesogens, both in the monomeric and polymeric state.

the metallo-supramolecular chemistry of these mesogens is highly sensitive to the length of the alkyl chains and the size of the core, which is a result of the delicate balance between the intermolecular interactions of the ligands and the intramolecular forces of the mesogens.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liquid crystalline properties can be tuned by the choice of the aromatic core of the ligand.

the liquid crystalline behavior of the monomer and the resulting oligomer or polymer is dictated by the length of the alkyl substituets, and the metal ion binding properties of the mesogens are dictated by the size of the central aromatic core.
the metallo-responsive liquid crystalline behavior is not dependent on polymerization.
